title: Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery — Notice-Age Rates on Repayment Plan Installments
content:
The age of a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** sets a notice rate on the monthly installment of a direct-payment repayment plan.

**Rule.** When the notice is no more than the waiver window in calendar days old and the debt carries no fraud, misrepresentation or bad faith finding, the recent-notice rate of 98 percent applies. When the notice is older than the waiver window but no more than 365 calendar days old and there is no such finding, the one-year rate of 99 percent applies. Otherwise no notice rate applies.

The notice age is counted in calendar days from the notice date on the debt record to today. The finding is read from the debt record. The notice rate is a percentage by which the quotient of the balance to be spread and the months is multiplied before the installment is rounded up to the cent.

| Debt type | Waiver window (calendar days after the notice) |
|---|---|
| Education Overpayment (Chapters 30, 35 and 1606) | 180 |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill Housing and Books Overpayment | 180 |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill Tuition and Fees Overpayment | 180 |
| Disability Compensation Overpayment | 180 |
| Veterans Pension Overpayment | 180 |
| Home Loan Guaranty Debt | 365 |

For a Home Loan Guaranty Debt the waiver window is itself 365 days, so no notice age falls between the window and 365 days.

## Truth table

| Notice age | Fraud, misrepresentation or bad faith finding | Notice rate |
|---|---|---|
| Within the waiver window | No | 98 percent |
| Older than the window, no more than 365 days | No | 99 percent |
| More than 365 days | No | None |
| Any | Yes | None |

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, Disability Compensation Overpayment).** Notice 180 days old: 98 percent. 181 days: 99 percent. 365 days: 99 percent. 366 days: none.
